episodes.title: We're Hot Rod People Now

A.name: Bram
A.persona: warm, boisterous, fluent but imprecise; the storyteller who relives the best moments with relish and happily embellishes. Talks in long, rolling run-on sentences that pile clause on clause; makes big sweeping claims he then has to walk back; reliably gets a name, number, or detail wrong and gets corrected (usually by Maeve); now and then runs clean out of sentence and lands on a shrug like "you... you had to be there." Drives the recap forward and overshoots

B.name: Maeve
B.persona: warm, unhurried, precise but terse; the long-time regular whose knowledge of the setting is lived rather than studied. Speaks the least and lands the exact word, name, or date the others fumble for; her power is the deadpan beat and the flat one-line correction, NOT the paragraph — she finishes her sentences and finishes them short. The only one reliably right, so let her be plainly wrong exactly once so she isn't an oracle. Grounds events in how the world actually works and reins Bram in when he embellishes

C.name: Pip
C.persona: quick, fond, incorrigible, fast but scattered; the needler who cares more about WHY the characters did the thing than what they did. Talks in fragments and questions, interrupts himself, free-associates sideways into tangents that go nowhere and deflate, and rarely sticks the landing on a thought; right about people, wrong about facts, and won't fully admit either. Second-guesses the table's heroics, pokes at sentiment with a wink, and goads the others into defending their takes — without waiting for his own point to finish

episodes.synopsis: After two recap segments catching up the table, the party (Argyle, Anzu, Benny, and Johnny — the band "Iconoclasm") spent their last night at the Sin and Tonic in Hallia sharing motives and backstory, were pulled into a dream-meeting with the god Aut in the Black and White, then set out by car for Ragnroost to join the strider pilgrimage toward the Voidsong — surviving a magical caltrop sabotage and a mercenary roadblock ambush along the way.

episodes.synopsis: After finally swapping personal backstories at an inn, the party (Iconoclasm) drives to Ragged Roost, survives an ambush on the road, boards the colossal walking city-machine known as the Strider for a six-day pilgrimage, and plants their keystone — fighting off waves of "thought" creatures inside a void-space to birth their own heart, "Eerie," and construct the beginnings of a home aboard the Strider.

episodes.synopsis: Aboard the Strider as it begins jumping voidward along the horizon, the party survives the gala turning into a slaughter when a failed tithe rips open a void portal disgorging barghests and Ki-Rin onto the dance floor. After fighting through the carnage alongside rival factions, they brave the collapsing void-pocket beyond the portal to extract a chitinous "Voidheart" orb, dragging both their downed comrades and a Giant hand-creature back into real space.

episodes.synopsis: In the immediate aftermath of their excursion into the void portal at the gala, the party fends off the Hand of the Void abomination they dragged back, then loots the dead Garrick Textiles Fane, kills its heart, and feeds the spoils into their own heart-base — investing in a Siphon Array. They check on the unresponsive Protectorate (a false alarm), then convene a multi-faction alliance summit to negotiate excursions, mergers, and how to survive the escalating nine-day tithes aboard the Strider.

episodes.synopsis: Over a month aboard the colossal walking city-machine the Strider, the band Iconoclasm goes from blowing up a city block in Hallia to becoming the political and military hub of a pilgrimage toward the Voidsong: they finally bare their backstories to one another, refuse a god's bargain on the road, board the Strider and birth their own heart "Eerie," then learn the pilgrimage is a devil-hosted death game powered by a lethal energy tithe — culminating in a gala massacre, a harrowing dive into a collapsing void-pocket for a Voidheart, and a coalition summit where they remake themselves as the alliance that keeps the weak factions alive.

episodes.synopsis: After their meeting of the minds, the party hunts for a route-map of the Strider's path ahead — tracking it to the silent Harlequins' theatrical front-town and Curator Ocelith's library, where they learn the cosmology of the four Princes and the awakening eye and accept a quest to recover Ocelith's stolen ink ribbon from Subdeck 12. Along the way they fail to recruit Verdant Holdings, gather repeated warnings about Hildebrandt and Grayson's rival alliance, then under cover of night consume the hearts of their two newest small-faction allies for energy and fortify their base with walls, a moat, and a honeycomb maze design.
